Frequently Asked Questions

1. What makes lead generation challenging for industrial automation and engineering firms?

Developing leads for industrial automation and engineering firms can be challenging due not only to long sales cycles but also because of multiple levels of purchasing authority and the technical nature of the products being sold. In addition, industrial automation customers generally need to see detailed information before they will proceed to purchase, and thus, responding to generic outreach is usually less productive than more personalized outreach methods.

2. Who are the key decision-makers in industrial automation purchases?

Three groups of individuals typically make final decisions on purchasing industrial automation solutions: plant managers, operations managers, and systems integrators; all have different criteria for making their final decisions based on technical fit, cost, and long-term viability.

3. How can engineering firms attract the right kind of prospects?

An engineering firm can effectively reach its target industry by creating communications that speak to the target market, using multiple channels of communication, and providing content that helps identify solutions to the problems of its potential customers.

4. What type of outreach works best in industrial automation sales?

A blended approach that includes email, LinkedIn, and direct outreach would be the best approach to use. Constantly sending out several personal messages through multiple channels would help build relationships and increase trust in comparison to just randomly sending out messages at some point in time.

5. Why is alignment between sales and marketing important in this industry?

Sales and marketing teams being aligned makes it much easier to move prospects through the funnel. As marketing raises awareness and interest, sales convert interest into qualified sales leads, creating an overall more seamless process.
